chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muhammad ibn Talhah, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Trimming the nails, clipping the moustache, and washing the head with the khitmah (a type of plant) every Friday removes poverty and increases livelihood.

key_terms.الْخِطْمِيِّ: Kithmir (a specific plant used for washing)

ai.seo_question: What are the benefits of trimming nails and clipping the moustache on Friday according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) links these specific Friday grooming rituals to spiritual and material prosperity, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *fitrah* (natural disposition) and the sanctity of the weekly congregational day. The inclusion of washing the head with *khitmah* (a type of soap or cleansing agent) highlights the holistic nature of purification in Shia jurisprudence, where physical cleanliness is viewed as a means to attract divine bounty and ward off poverty.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muhammad Bin Talha who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Trimming of the nails and clipping of the moustache, and washing of the head with the hibiscus (plant) every Friday negates the poverty and increase in the livelihood’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Muhammad ibn Talhah who has said the following: “
Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Clipping fingernails, mustache and washing one’s head with hollyhock (marshmallow plant) every Friday banishes poverty and increases one’s sustenance.’”
